title: Saving a new part number renames the part in place
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), with 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete' and See Financial Data.
  • You can switch to a second location, {Location-B} (for example Staging Lethbridge - 4310), in the location switcher in the top bar.
  • Part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-RENAME-01), with the description {Description-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST PL Rename) and a Core Charge (for example 15.00), is stocked at {Location-A} with 3 on hand in its default bin {Bin-A} (for example General Storage).
  • {Part-A}'s core, {Core-A} (for example "Core for ZZAUTOTEST PL Rename"), comes from its Core Charge and has its own Part History page.
  • {Part-A} is also stocked at {Location-B}, on the same Part Library entry.
  • {Part-A} at {Location-A} already has an earlier Part History entry (for example a Sell Price change from 20.00 to 21.00).
  • The new number, {Number-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-RENAMED-02), is used by no part and no Part Library entry.
custom_steps:
1. At {Location-A}, go to Parts → Inventory and type {Part-A} in the search.
  2. Click the {Part-A} row.
  3. Replace the Part Number with {Number-A}.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Type {Number-A} in the Inventory search.
  6. Click the clock icon (Part History) on the {Number-A} row.
  7. Go to Parts → Part Library and type {Part-A} in the search.
  8. Type {Number-A} in the Part Library search.
  9. Click the {Number-A} row.
  10. Open the Part History page of {Core-A}.
  11. Pick {Location-B} in the location switcher.
  12. Go to Parts → Inventory and type {Number-A} in the search.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 4: the window closes and the change is saved.
  • Step 4: a number or description change made through the public API, instead of this window, follows the same rules as this window. This part cannot be checked by hand; write "not checked by hand" in the result comment.
  • Step 5: one row shows {Number-A} with {Description-A} and the same bin {Bin-A} with quantity 3, unchanged.
  • Step 6: Part History still shows the earlier entry, plus a new entry "Part number updated | Original number: {Part-A} | New number: {Number-A}": it is the same part, with its history kept.
  • Step 7: no entry has the number {Part-A} any more.
  • Step 8: exactly one entry has {Number-A}: no new entry was made.
  • Step 9: the entry's page lists both {Location-A} and {Location-B} under Workplace.
  • Step 10: {Core-A}'s own Part History page shows Part number {Number-A} and the entry "Part number updated | Original number: {Part-A} | New number: {Number-A}": the core took the same number. If no screen lets you open {Core-A}'s own Part History page, write "not checked by hand" for this step in the result comment.
  • Step 12: at {Location-B} the part also reads {Number-A}.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, v29 (14 Oct 2026 copy), S13-R18, S13-R19d, S10-R23, S10-R26, S5-E3, read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas board 2.2 (Both fields edited), board 2.3 (Saved: the list shows the new values), board 2.4 (Part History at Heavy Duty), board 2.5 (Lethbridge: renamed there too), 13 Oct copy. Product's answer of 13 Oct (Chris Ward, question 6). Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S13-R18: “Saving a changed number renames the part in place. The part keeps its identity, its history, and every line that holds it. Its Part Library entry is renamed with it, and its core takes the same number. No new Part Library entry is created.”
  • S10-R23: “A changed part number writes "Part number updated | Original number: {old} | New number: {new}" to the Part History of the part at every location that stocks it.”
  • S13-R19d: “A change to a part's number or description made through the public API follows the same rules as the part dialog: S13-R14, S13-R15, S13-R18, S13-R19, S13-N1, S13-N7 and S10-R23 to S10-R25.”
  • S10-R26: “When the part has a core, the core gets the same number or description entry. The core's description entries read its own description, "Core for {description}".”
  • S5-E3: “A core has no row of its own on the Inventory list, in Export or on the Part Library list, so it cannot be ticked for a bulk change. Its name (S13-R15) and its history show on the core's own Part History page. The core reason in S10-R13a applies when a core reaches a status change by any other route.”
